status_summary: After the 90-day pause ordered on 2025-01-20, USAID's remaining operations were merged into the State Department on 2025-07-01, by which time NPR reported that more than 80 percent of USAID programs had been terminated. Congress enacted the Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28) on 2025-07-24, rescinding about 7.9 billion dollars of foreign assistance and related funds, including 2.5 billion dollars for Development Assistance, 1.65 billion dollars for the Economic Support Fund and 496 million dollars for International Disaster Assistance. After a special message of 2025-08-28 proposing to rescind further foreign aid funds and a district court order of 2025-09-03 requiring obligation of expiring aid funds, the Supreme Court on 2025-09-26 stayed that order as to the funds in the special message (a preliminary ruling, not on the merits; the docket shows no later entry and no D.C. Circuit merits ruling was found). The FY2026 appropriations law (Public Law 119-75, Division F, enacted 2026-02-03) provides 50.07 billion dollars net of rescissions for State and foreign operations, 3.5 percent below FY2025, against a request of 31.14 billion dollars plus 22.30 billion in proposed rescissions (CRS R48624); it carries no standalone Development Assistance or Economic Support Fund account, merges International Disaster Assistance and Migration and Refugee Assistance into a 5.40 billion dollar International Humanitarian Assistance account, and provides 174.5 million dollars for the former USAID administrative function. For comparison, CRS R45168 gives FY2019 enacted State and foreign operations funding of 54.38 billion dollars (46.40 billion excluding overseas contingency funds), USAID operating expenses of about 1.37 billion dollars and International Disaster Assistance of about 4.39 billion. Inference: in nominal dollars the FY2026 total sits below the FY2019 total and the USAID administrative line far below it, while the merged humanitarian account cannot be compared like for like with International Disaster Assistance. For FY2027, CRS describes a request of about 37.8 billion dollars, down about 27 percent from FY2026 enacted levels, and says the House passed H.R. 8595 on 2026-07-15 with about 49.2 billion dollars in new budget authority; it reports no Senate action. Inference: the program terminations and the end of USAID as a separate agency go further than the budget reduction the Mandate described.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14169 paused new obligations and disbursements of foreign development assistance for a 90-day review (published 2025-01-30 at 90 FR 8619).
USAID's remaining operations are merged into the State Department as the agency closes; NPR reported that more than 80 percent of USAID's programs had been terminated by then.

Public Law 119-28 (Rescissions Act of 2025) rescinded about $7.9 billion in foreign assistance and related funds, including Development Assistance $2.5 billion, Economic Support Fund $1.65 billion, Migration and Refugee Assistance $800 million, Global Health Programs $500 million, International Disaster Assistance $496 million and USAID operating expenses $125 million.
The President sent Congress a special message proposing to rescind additional foreign assistance funds; a district court issued an order on 2025-09-03 concerning the funds covered by that message.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-75, the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 7148), becomes law after House passage 341 to 88 (2026-01-22), Senate passage 71 to 29 (2026-01-30) and House agreement 217 to 214 (2026-02-03). Per CRS R48624, its Division F (National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs) provides 50.07 billion dollars net of rescissions, 3.5 percent below FY2025 enacted, provides no standalone Development Assistance or Economic Support Fund accounts, funds a new International Humanitarian Assistance account at 5.40 billion dollars, and provides 174.5 million dollars for Administration of Assistance, 90.9 percent below the FY2025 USAID administrative level.

The House passes H.R. 8595, FY2027 national security, State and related programs appropriations, with about 49.2 billion dollars in new budget authority, against an administration request of about 37.8 billion dollars (CRS); no Senate action reported as of the CRS report dated 2026-07-30.

title: Cut USAID and foreign aid spending toward 2019 levels and trim the 150 Account
uncertainties: The dollar size of the 2025-08-28 special message (commonly reported as several billion dollars) was not in the sources that could be opened, so it is not stated. P.L. 119-75 was confirmed through its govinfo.gov bill status record; the enrolled Division F text is too long for the fetch tool, so FY2026 amounts rest on CRS R48624 (updated 2026-07-15), a partly primary route. The FY2019 comparison uses CRS R45168 (updated 2019-03-25), in nominal dollars, for the State and foreign operations bill rather than the whole 150 Account; the FY2019 total includes 8.0 billion dollars of overseas contingency funds and it is not stated whether it is net of a 301 million dollar rescission. A WOLA analysis reports the FY2026 act as about 9.3 billion dollars below prior-year levels and almost 60 percent above a 31.5 billion dollar request; these figures use a different basis from CRS (3.5 percent below FY2025, request of 31.14 billion before rescissions) and the CRS figures are used. Not verified: GAO's view of the pocket rescission or the D.C. Circuit's ruling on the merits. The Rescissions Act total of about 7.9 billion dollars is the sum of foreign-assistance and related paragraphs 1 to 19 of section 2(b) (including international organization contributions); the Corporation for Public Broadcasting rescission is not included. The 2025-07-01 merger date and the share of terminated programs come from an NPR report; no State Department notice was read.
